name: Fit-focused dressing for body type (shoulder-to-waist illusion)
lead: Fit-focused dressing refers to choosing garment cuts that emphasise a V-shaped torso, with wide shoulders and a narrower waist, and that minimise features a wearer sees as flaws. The inverted-triangle (V) shape is one of the male body shape categories, described as wider shoulders and chest with a narrow waist.[1]

Wide shoulders and a muscular upper body are linked in the literature to perceived masculinity and attractiveness, and studies cited on Wikipedia found women rate lower waist-to-chest ratios in men as more desirable.[1]
No published trials have tested whether particular cuts of clothing change a man's rated attractiveness.
infobox: Emphasise a V-taper; de-emphasise perceived frame flaws

paras: Body shape is shaped by skeletal structure and by muscle and fat distribution; skeletal structure stops growing in the teen years while muscle and fat can change.[1] Men's shapes are commonly described as inverted triangle, rectangle or apple.[1]

Practitioners describe tailoring and fit choices intended to make shoulders look broader relative to the waist. Garment sizing in general is based on chest, waist and hip measurements, and posture affects those measurements.[1]
No studies found. Related research on body proportions and perceived attractiveness exists, but it concerns bodies rather than clothing fit.

card.summary: Cuts and fit chosen to show off a V-taper; popular in style advice, untested as a clothing intervention.
card.aka: V-taper dressing, tailoring for body type

quick.overview:
This is the practice of choosing clothing cut and fit to emphasise a broad-shoulder, narrow-waist look and downplay other areas.

Body-shape literature links wide shoulders and a narrow waist to perceived attractiveness, but no study has tested whether specific clothing cuts produce that effect.
quick.mechanism: Fit and tailoring change where garments sit and how much volume they add, which practitioners say alters the apparent shoulder-to-waist proportion.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented for ordinary clothing choices.
